speaker: Doctor
text: I see you're experiencing fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes. These symptoms together are concerning for a systemic illness, possibly malignancy or infection. To help narrow this down, can you tell me how long these symptoms have been present and if you've noticed any fevers or changes in your skin?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the rapid progression of weight loss and night sweats over just four weeks, this raises significant concern for lymphoma or metastatic disease. Have you experienced any fevers, and has anyone noticed a new lump or swelling elsewhere on your body? Also, do you have a history of smoking or recent infections?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Lymphoma (likely Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma). The combination of B-symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss), rapidly enlarging fixed supraclavicular lymph nodes, and abdominal pain strongly suggests a systemic malignancy. I am requesting a CT of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis along with a biopsy of the supraclavicular node. REQUEST TEST: CT_Chest_Abdomen_Pelvis; REQUEST TEST: Lymph_Node_Biopsy; REQUEST IMAGES
